target: route "treewidth": Bounded width — a seventh polynomial class, or the exact place where interface tables explode (results tw:response, tw:fold-width, tw:one-live, tw:no-clock, tw:cut-sign, tw:tarski, tw:round/tw:recover, tw:modulator, tw:colour-feedback, tw:qp, tw:cyclic, tw:family, tw:gap2-shape)

findings.defect: The proposition is FALSE as stated: its hypothesis derives stopping from digraph reachability ("from every internal vertex of which an input is reachable, so that Lambda with its inputs read as terminals is a stopping payoff game"), and that implication is false; under the literal hypotheses both the additive-homogeneity identity and the conclusion Phi_1-Phi_2 = psi(f-g) fail.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-treewidth-correctness/t_noclock.py, exact lfp arithmetic. (a) Gadget A: internal v1 Min->(v1,i_f), v2 Min->(v2,i_g), outputs v1,v2. Every internal vertex has both successors among internal+input vertices and reaches an input, so the stated hypotheses hold; but {v1} is a nonempty trap, the game is NOT stopping, and lfp gives Phi==(0,0), so Phi(f+c,g+c)=(0,0) while Phi(f,g)+c=(1/4,1/4) at c=1/4. (b) Gadget B: z Min->(z,i_f) [lfp value 0 -- a HARD CONSTANT manufactured with no terminal read], h avg->(i_f,z), m Max->(i_f,i_g), q Min->(i_f,h), outputs m,q. Hypotheses again hold literally; Phi_1-Phi_2 = max(f,g)-f/2, which is not a function of f-g: at (f,g)=(0,0) it is 0, at (f,g)=(1,1) it is 1/2, same difference d=0. So the conclusion fails. Gadget B also refutes the stated moral ("a fold that accumulates requires the gadget to read a terminal") in the non-stopping regime. Repair: replace the reachability clause by the hypothesis that Lambda with inputs read as terminals is stopping -- free in the GAP-2 context, since a sub-gadget of a stopping game is stopping (its traps are traps of the whole game). NOTE the standing trap: the route's verification ran on 3000 gadgets "all of them acyclic, hence stopping", i.e. the parameter the proposition turns on was constant across the entire test set, which is exactly why the falsity was not seen.

findings.defect: Both theorems close with an "In particular" clause that drops the standing stopping hypothesis and asserts decidability of SSG-Value/prob:main, which is posed for ARBITRARY SSGs (frontier.tex l.277); the clause is false, and the advertised self-certification T(w)=w does not detect the error.
findings.evidence: Rebuilt both algorithms from the statements (/tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-treewidth-correctness/qp.py, modulator.py). (a) tw:qp, t_nonstop3.py: the SSG on u_1..u_10 all AVERAGE with u_i->(u_{i+1},u_{i+1}) cyclically (N=12, a=10, treewidth 2, greatest trap = all 10 vertices, so non-stopping) has val==0 everywhere (brute force max_sigma min_tau over lfp pair values); the separator+Tarski recursion returns 1/2 at every vertex and g.certify(T(w)=w) returns True. (b) tw:modulator, t_nonstop4.py: u_1..u_8 alternately Max/average with u_i->(u_{i+1},u_{i+1}) cyclically (N=10, non-stopping, mu_max=1 attained by X={h}=... {u_1}, freezing u_1 leaves an acyclic hence max-acyclic game) has val==0; the modulator algorithm returns 1/2 everywhere after 1 cut-map query and T(w)=w passes. Root cause: without stopping, lem:cut only gives val|_S = lfp(F_S); tw:cut-sign's UNIQUENESS and thm:contraction's uniqueness of the fixed point of T both need stopping, so the Tarski search can return a non-least fixed point and the certificate is vacuous. Consequences: (i) tw:qp's sentence "SSG-Value restricted to any family of treewidth O(1) is decidable in quasipolynomial time N^{O(log N)}, and the algorithm certifies its own output by checking Tw=w" and tw:modulator's "In particular prob:main is decidable in polynomial time on every family with mu_P = O(1), and in time N^{O(mu)} in general" must both carry "stopping"; (ii) the claim that tw:modulator "answers the question rem:kacyclic explicitly leaves open" is answered only for stopping games, whereas thm:kacyclic (the mu_k=0 case) is explicitly proved with NO stopping hypothesis; (iii) recovering the general case needs the unproved statement "thm:stopping-transform preserves bounded treewidth and bounded mu_P". The corollary tw:kacyclic-mu is correctly stated ("stopping SSG") and is unaffected.

findings.defect: Systematic citation gap: four frontier.tex results stated only for SSGs (two sinks, payoffs 0 and 1) are used throughout for general PAYOFF games (arbitrarily many terminals, arbitrary rational payoffs), and the only justification offered covers something else.
findings.evidence: tw:round writes "By thm:contraction -- whose proof compares two finite-horizon games that differ only in the terminal payoff function, so it holds verbatim for payoff games (lem:gen-comparison)"; but lem:gen-comparison (frontier.tex l.10686) is about an SSG with its two sinks re-paid alpha<beta, not about a payoff game with many terminals. The same silent extension is made for thm:stopping-determinacy (in tw:response(b) and in tw:qp's brute-force base case), cor:comparison (in tw:cut-sign) and lem:denominator-sharp (in tw:recover, where det A_U <= 2^a is quoted from a lemma proved only for sink payoffs 0,1). The extensions are TRUE -- I verified the payoff-game denominator bound Delta*2^a on 3699 coordinates of 400 random stopping payoff games with 2-4 terminals of denominators 1,2,3,4,5,8, together with 400 fixed-point checks, 2400 sign-implication checks, 2400 monotonicity and 2400 sup-norm-Lipschitz checks and full-payoff-vector shift-equivariance, 0 failures (t_cutsign.py) -- but they are not in the document. MISSING STATEMENT, one sentence: "thm:contraction, thm:stopping-determinacy, cor:comparison and lem:denominator-sharp hold verbatim for stopping payoff games in the sense of def:payoff, with the denominator bound Delta*2^a where Delta is a common denominator of the terminal payoffs."

findings.defect: "mu_k <= f_k always ... so tw:modulator applies whenever tw:colour-feedback does" is false: tw:colour-feedback is proved for arbitrary SSGs, stopping or not, while tw:modulator requires stopping.
findings.evidence: The very instance of the previous finding separates them: the 10-vertex alternating Max/average cycle has f_max=4 and mu_max=1; the 2^{f_max} enumeration of tw:colour-feedback returns the correct value 0 (each G_rho is a cycle of average vertices, max_rho val = 0), while tw:modulator returns 1/2. I also validated tw:colour-feedback itself on 200 random SSGs, both colours, 173 of them NOT stopping, 0 mismatches against brute-force max-min over lfp pair values (t_colour.py); the theorem is correct as stated.

findings.defect: The piece index is off by one: val(u) does not lie in "the 2^{D-1}-st of 2^D" intervals but in the (2^{D-1}+1)-st (0-based index j = 2^{D-1}), the interval immediately above 1/2.
findings.evidence: t_cyc.py: val(u) = 1/2 + 3*2^{-(D+3)} = (2^{D-1} + 3/8)*2^{-D} for 2<=D<=12 (formula verified exactly, all matches), so floor(val(u)*2^D) = 2^{D-1}. Everything else in tw:cyclic reproduces exactly: P_D^circ is stopping, every cycle meets u, freezing u leaves an acyclic game, and the route's explicit layout with u added has width 5 (pw<=5) with tw=pw=4 at D=3 (exact DP) -- I additionally find tw=pw=5 at D=4.

findings.defect: The reported query count "ten at D=1" is not reproducible from the specification; a from-scratch implementation of the same recipe gives eleven. The other counts reproduce exactly.
findings.evidence: t_mod.py (independent implementation of eps = 1/(4N 2^a Q^2), Q = Delta*2^a, B = ceil(log2(1/eps)), round-up grid, tw:tarski verbatim): P_D^circ with X={u} takes 4 cut-map evaluations for 2<=D<=12 (route: 4) but 11 at D=1 (route: 10); M_n with X={h} takes 10 for 2<=n<=5 and 11 for 6<=n<=12, matching the route's "10 or 11 for every 2<=n<=12". findings.defect: "the exact values of tw=pw are 2 for H_m and for G_m ..., 3 for the ladder L_n" is false at the smallest parameter of the route's own measured range (3<=m<=8, 3<=n<=8).

findings.defect: The one-line derivation of the balanced separator is not well defined as written: "orient every edge of the decomposition tree towards the side carrying more than n/2 vertices, take a node all of whose incident edges point to it" leaves an edge unoriented whenever neither side carries strictly more than n/2 vertices, so the chosen node need not exist by that recipe.
findings.evidence: Textual. The underlying lemma (a bag X, |X|<=k+1, whose removal leaves components of at most n/2 vertices) is standard and true; only the derivation is incomplete. My implementation sidesteps it by brute-force search over subsets of size <= k+1 (qp.py, balanced_separator), which always found one on all 330 test games.

findings.defect: The theorem takes the modulator X as given; the corollary's bound N^{O(mu_k)} silently absorbs the search for X and the membership test, neither of which is stated.
findings.evidence: tw:modulator: "let X attain it". tw:kacyclic-mu: "computable exactly in time N^{O(mu_k)}". For P = A_k the search is N^{O(mu_k)} subsets each tested in polynomial time (a cycle-hitting check), so the bound survives, but the step is asserted. The route's own next_steps item 3 flags recognition as an open question, which is inconsistent with quoting the corollary as a checkable class.

findings.defect: log(1/lambda) <= t/(1-t) is the natural-logarithm bound, while thm:escape-class's running time is stated with log_2(1/lambda); the conclusion loses a factor ln 2.
findings.evidence: thm:escape-class (frontier.tex l.1566) gives O(N + (a + log_2 kappa)/log_2(1/lambda)). With t < 4*2^{-n} one gets log_2(1/lambda) < 2^{-n+3}/ln 2, so the bound is at least a*ln2*2^{n-3}, still 2^{Omega(N)}. The rest of (viii) is correct: I verified the necessary chain u_1=1, u_{i+1} <= 2*lambda*u_i - 1, u_i>0 dies for every n=3..12 at lambda = 1-4*2^{-n} (t_esc.py), and the true threshold rho of the c-part survival matrix satisfies 1-rho ~ 2^{-n}, comfortably inside the proved bound.

verdict:
Not sound. Two major defects survive; the rest of the route reproduces exactly.

WHAT HOLDS. I rebuilt every numerical claim from the statements (not from the route's code) in exact rational arithmetic, with my own game core, my own exact treewidth/pathwidth DPs, my own piecewise-affine engine, and my own implementations of tw:tarski, tw:modulator and tw:qp. All of it reproduces: thm:fold's identity and the exact piece count 2^D with pi(A)=2^D and 2^D pairwise distinct optimal pairs; tw(P_D)=pw(P_D)=2,3,3,4 at D=1..4 with pw<=4 for every D by the route's explicit layout and pw>3 for 4<=D<=12; P_D^circ's value 1/2+3*2^{-(D+3)}, pw<=5, tw=pw=4 at D=3, and four cut-map queries for 2<=D<=12; M_n's stopping, reachability, values, denominator 2^{n+1}, alphabet n+3, mu_max=1, fvs>min(n,5), single Max-SCC, d=n+1, escape threshold, and 10-or-11 queries; tw:tarski's correctness and query bound; tw:cut-sign, tw:round, tw:response and the payoff-game denominator bound on 400 random stopping payoff games; tw:one-live's piece bound; tw:colour-feedback on 200 random SSGs of which 173 are NOT stopping; and tw:qp on 330 fresh random stopping SSGs of exact treewidth 2 and 3 with the base case lowered to force depth-3 recursion, 0 mismatches, 0 certification retries. The core mathematics of the route -- the table/search dichotomy, the seventh class, and the quasipolynomial bound for STOPPING games of bounded treewidth -- survives adversarial checking.

WHAT BREAKS. (1) tw:no-clock is false as stated. It derives "stopping" from "an input is reachable from every internal vertex", which is not a valid implication, and under its literal hypotheses both the additive-homogeneity identity and the conclusion Phi_1-Phi_2=psi(f-g) fail; explicit four-vertex witness with a Min self-loop that manufactures a hard constant 0 without reading any terminal, refuting the stated moral too. Its 3000-gadget verification used only ACYCLIC gadgets, i.e. held the parameter it turns on constant across the whole test set -- the project's standing measurement trap. Repair: hypothesise stopping directly; that is free in the GAP-2 context, so the GAP-2 narrowing survives.
(2) tw:qp and tw:modulator each end with an "In particular ... SSG-Value / prob:main is decidable ..." clause that drops the standing stopping hypothesis. prob:main is posed for arbitrary SSGs. I exhibit a 12-vertex non-stopping SSG of treewidth 2 on which the tw:qp recursion returns 1/2 everywhere for a game of value 0 and the advertised T(w)=w certificate passes, and a 10-vertex non-stopping SSG with mu_max=1 on which tw:modulator does the same. The cause is exactly that lem:cut alone gives only the LEAST fixed point of F_S; uniqueness -- and the value of the certificate -- is tw:cut-sign's, and needs stopping. This also means the claim to have answered rem:kacyclic is limited to the stopping case, whereas thm:kacyclic itself is proved with no stopping hypothesis.

Beyond those, one systematic minor gap runs through the route: thm:contraction, thm:stopping-determinacy, cor:comparison and lem:denominator-sharp are stated in frontier.tex only for SSGs with sinks t_0,t_1, and are used throughout for general payoff games; the justification offered (lem:gen-comparison) covers a different generalisation. The generalisations are true and I verified their consequences numerically, but they need to be stated.

NOT CHECKED: the literature claims in tw:literature and tw:tarski-prior (no network access), and tw:gap2-shape's two searches, which are not reproducible from the statement as written and are correctly labelled "measured".
